name: Comparing two or more
rule: Comparing two things: -er or 'more' (taller, more careful).
Comparing three or more: -est or 'most' (tallest, most careful).

wrong.text: This road is busiest than the one near school.

right.text: This road is busier than the one near school.

spot: 'Than' after it means two things: use the -er or 'more' form.
deeper: Short words take -er: big → bigger. Long words take 'more': more beautiful.
Odd ones: good → better → best; bad → worse → worst.
